description:
My name is Curtis Hayes. I spent thirty-one years in a security uniform,  night shifts at a mall starting in '88, years in loss prevention learning to read people on camera, and the last stretch running the desk of a residential high-rise, watching strangers walk up to doors for a living. Here's what all that footage taught me: nobody ever picked a building because the alarm was cheap. They picked it because the house told them everything before they touched the handle.

That's what these videos are. The small giveaways a stranger reads off your door, your porch, your routine,  and the fifteen-dollar way to shut each one down. I did the job; I'm not selling you a system. If it costs more than a bag of groceries, I'll say so and usually talk you out of it.

Every comment gets read by me, nobody else. If you worked a door, a gate, or a graveyard shift and know a trick I haven't covered, put it down there,  that's where my best episodes start.
